findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Sequence F10 and F12 explicitly (or require the later one to rebase and regenerate `overview.txt` and the CLI reference under the merged generator) since both regenerate and drift-check the same committed CLI artifacts.
evidence: F10 plan: 'Regenerate packaged import help, overview help, and the CLI reference.' and AC 'Overview help carries the canonical import summary.' + 'python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check confirms the CLI reference matches the canonical source.'

F12 plan: 'Move `_unwrap_usage` and `_collapse_metavars` from scripts/gen_cli_reference.py into scripts/gen_cli_help.py ... Apply metavar normalization ... before byte normalization' and 'Generate one committed artifact for each newly help-backed route and regenerate `overview.txt`' and 'Delete `_render_intercept` from scripts/gen_cli_reference.py. Make CLI reference generation consume `subcommand_help(route.name)` for every documented route.'
F12 changes the generator normalization and the committed overview.txt/CLI-reference bytes that F10 also regenerates and drift-checks against the same committed bytes.
findings.finding: F10 (c679) and F12 (65c9) both regenerate and commit the same generated CLI artifacts (overview help `overview.txt`, the external CLI reference) through the same generators (`scripts/gen_cli_help.py`, `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`), yet neither child names the other or states any rebase/ordering discipline for these shared generated files.
scenarios: F12 lands after F10: F12's generator-normalization rewrite changes overview.txt/CLI-reference bytes, invalidating F10's just-regenerated committed artifacts and its drift-check assumptions.
F10 lands after F12: F10 must regenerate under F12's new metavar/usage normalization; if F10 was authored against the pre-F12 generator, its committed bytes and `--check` will disagree with main.
findings.suggested_fix: State an ordering constraint (land F12's generator rewrite first, then rebase F10 onto it and regenerate) or note in both children that the later change must regenerate overview help and the CLI reference against the merged `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`/`gen_cli_reference.py`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State F20's auth/permission precondition: performing the GitHub About-description edit (via `gh repo edit navapbc/rebar --description`, equivalently `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}`) requires an authenticated gh session or token with repository-administration (admin) rights on navapbc/rebar, and readback verification uses the same authenticated read path.
evidence: The mechanism is achievable and already used in-repo: infra/runbooks/github-mirror-lock.md:213 uses `gh repo edit navapbc/rebar --description "..."` to set the About description (so `gh repo edit --description` MATCHES the intended surface; feasibility is Verified).

ABSENCE: neither the Plan nor the Acceptance Criteria names the command/endpoint (`gh repo edit --description` or REST `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}`) nor states that the write needs admin/repo-administration permission on navapbc/rebar.
T3 checklist item (c) 'Auth/HTTPS preconditions stated' is not satisfied for the F20 metadata write; the surface is HTTPS via the GitHub API but the required admin scope is unstated.
findings.finding: F20 asserts a GitHub repository-metadata write (edit the About description) plus exact readback verification but never states the auth/permission precondition that write requires (an authenticated gh session or token with repository-administration/admin rights on navapbc/rebar).
findings.location: Plan bullet 'Update GitHub About metadata to lead with enforceable plan review and signed completion verification'; AC 'F20 updates the GitHub About description without changing repository files, topics, or homepage' and 'The GitHub metadata child passes plan review and exact readback verification before close'
scenarios: The executing agent/operator runs the F20 change with a token or gh session lacking repo-admin rights and the About-description update silently fails or is rejected, blocking close after the doc-side work is complete.
Readback verification cannot be performed or is ambiguous because the acting principal was never scoped to read/write repository settings.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a precondition line to F20 naming the mechanism and scope, e.g. 'F20 uses `gh repo edit navapbc/rebar --description` under an authenticated gh session with repository-administration rights on navapbc/rebar; it sets only --description and leaves topics, homepage, and files unchanged; readback verification re-reads the About description over the same authenticated GitHub API.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the 'both Gerrit gates before merge' assurance is intended to be framework-enforced per child rather than restated in each repository child's AC.
evidence: Repository children assert local checks only, e.g. F08A 'The recorded D1 through D4 verification commands pass'; F10 focused pytest + gen `--check`; F13 'Generated-reference and focused MCP tests pass'; F19 'All children pass applicable targeted checks and land independently.'
No repository child's AC block names 'both Gerrit gates' / plan-review + completion-verifier passage; only F20 (71fe), the non-repository child, references plan review at the child level.
This is the covered-by-definition boundary: Gerrit-gate passage is a framework-enforced landing precondition for every child, so it is structural rather than a hard uncovered gap.

scenarios: A reader auditing whether each repository child independently guarantees Gerrit-gate passage finds only local-check assertions in the child AC blocks.
